candidates.review_note: Generate the lexicographically smallest binary deBruijn cycle by concatenating lexicographically ordered Lyndon words whose lengths divide n. The requested value is the cyclic n-bit window beginning at k; cache cycles by n.

Enumerate distinct palindromic substrings by center expansion. Sort them by descending length. If every adjacent shorter string is contained in its predecessor, transitivity makes all comparable; otherwise that adjacent pair witnesses two distinct non-containing palindromes.

Maintain a bitset of attainable weights for each selected-item count. Descending count updates use each spaceship part at most once. Queries list all attainable counts in ascending order, including the empty subset at weightzero.
Flow conservation around the ring fixes every edge flow up to one common offset. Prefix inventory imbalances give those flows, and minimizing their absolute sum chooses a median offset.

Process values in sequence order. The best chain ending at x extends the best earlier chain ending at any divisor of x, including x itself. Factor values using primes up to their square root, enumerate divisors, and cache repeated factorizations.

Logical equivalence is strong connectivity of the implication graph. Contract strongly connected components using iterative Kosaraju; if more than one remains, the minimum added edges is the maximum of source and sink counts in the condensation DAG.

Subtractive Euclid preserves the gcd, which is the common terminal value. DP counts nonempty subsequences by their gcd; each new element either stays excluded, starts a singleton, or extends an earlier subsequence. Python integers retain the exact up-to2^60 count.

Maintain the set of seen one-character and two-character subsequences as bitsets. On each new character, first extend old pairs into distinct triples ending in that character, then old singles into pairs, preventing one position from being reused.
